Lithium ion battery

Technical Field

The invention belongs to the field of chemical power supplies, and particularly relates to a lithium ion battery.

Background

At present, taking a lithium ion battery taking lithium iron phosphate as an example of a positive electrode active material, the long cycle is about 3000 times. However, for the application of energy storage and commercial vehicle direction, the lithium iron cycle performance needs to be improved, but the current technology is difficult to realize.

One of the capacity losses during the current cycling is the leaching of metal ions from the positive electrode material. For example, iron ions are dissolved out from lithium iron phosphate, and particularly, in the high-temperature cycle process, the dissolution of positive iron is serious. And the electrolyte is deposited on the surface of the negative electrode, so that the decomposition of an SEI film of the negative electrode is accelerated, and the loss of active lithium is caused. Therefore, protection of the cathode material is crucial.

At present, the common methods for protecting the anode material include (1) coating inorganic substances such as carbon on the surface of the anode material during synthesis, or increasing the coating amount, which undoubtedly increases the production cost and reduces the compaction density of the material; (2) the electrolyte is added with the film forming additive, but the cost of the film forming additive is higher.

Disclosure of Invention

In order to overcome the defects, the invention provides a lithium ion battery.

The invention provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive electrode and electrolyte; the positive electrode comprises a positive active material and a metal M, wherein the metal M is a metal of which ions can be complexed with anions of lithium salt in the electrolyte, and the weight content of the metal M is 0.01-0.2% of the weight of the positive active material.

The invention provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive electrode, a negative electrode and an electrolyte, wherein the positive electrode comprises a positive active material and MmAnWherein M isn+Being capable of reacting with the lithium salt in the electrolyteAnion-complexed metal ions, Am-Is the anion of the lithium salt in the electrolyte, n is 1, 2 or 3, and m is 1 or 2; the M ismAnThe M is arranged on the surface of the anode in the lithium ion batterymAnThe content of the metal M is 0.01-0.2% of the weight of the positive active material.

According to the invention, the metal M is added into the positive electrode, and can be complexed with anions in the electrolyte in the first charge-discharge process, so that the protective film is formed on the surfaces of the positive electrode and the negative electrode, the corrosion of the positive electrode active material is prevented, the active lithium ions can be released, and the cycle performance of the battery is improved. Meanwhile, an SEI film can be formed on the negative electrode to protect the surface of the negative electrode from further corrosion, and the damage of metal ions dissolved out of the positive electrode to the SEI film of the negative electrode is weakened in the long-cycle process of the battery, so that the cycle performance is further improved. The invention can also arrange M on the surface of the positive electrodemAnThe above effects are also achieved, and the cycle performance is improved. The method is simple, high in operability and low in cost.

Detailed Description

The present invention will be described in detail with reference to the following embodiments.

One embodiment of the present invention provides a lithium ion battery, including a positive electrode and an electrolyte; the positive electrode comprises a positive active material and a metal M, wherein the weight content of the metal M is 0.01-0.2% of the weight of the positive active material.

By adding a certain amount of M, a CEI film can be formed on the surface of the positive electrode and an SEI film can be formed on the surface of the negative electrode in the first charge-discharge process, and the specific film forming mechanism is as follows.

During charging, the metal M will be oxidized to Mn+(n is 1, 2 or 3) and releases n electrons, most M ions can be neutralized with anions in the electrolyte (A)m-M is 1 or 2) in combination, e.g. LiPF6PF in lithium (hexafluorophosphate)6-Form M (PF)6)nAnd deposited on the surface of the positive electrode to form a compound similar to a CEI film, so as to protect the active material of the positive electrode and avoid the dissolution of metal ions in the active material.

A part of M ions is dissolved in the electrolyteIn the case where the compound M is transferred to a negative electrode like lithium ions, the compound M forms an SEI film-like film on the negative electrodemAnThe metal ion-exchange membrane is equivalent to a negative electrode membrane forming additive, so that the surface of a negative electrode is protected from further corrosion, and the damage of metal ions dissolved out of a positive electrode to a negative electrode SEI (solid electrolyte interphase) membrane is weakened in the long cycle process of a battery, so that the cycle performance is improved.

In addition, electrons released by oxidation of M migrate to the graphite negative electrode through an external circuit, and in order to maintain charge conservation, lithium salt is bonded to M due to anions in the electrolyte, and Li cation+Will pass through the electrolyte/separator to the negative electrode and combine with electrons to form a carbon-lithium alloy with the negative electrode graphite, i.e. LixCyAnd the lithium supplement effect can be realized. Since M has a strong conductive ability, the residual metal M powder can also enhance the electron conductivity of the positive electrode. Lithium salt LiPF is consumed due to the lithium supplement process6Therefore, LiPF in the electrolyte is preferable6The concentration of the lithium salt is 1.1-1.5mol/L higher than that of the lithium salt in the electrolyte of the common lithium ion battery.

The reaction equation is as follows:

xM+LiPF6-nxe--nxLi+→xM(PF6)n+(1-nx)LiPF6

xLi++xe-+Cy→LixCy

the inventive concept of the present invention is explained above by taking the lithium salt in the electrolyte as lithium hexafluorophosphate as an example, and from the above mechanism, those skilled in the art can understand that the object of the present invention can be achieved when the lithium salt in the electrolyte is other lithium salts suitable for lithium ion batteries.

In an alternative embodiment, the positive active material may be selected from one or more of lithium iron phosphate, lithium manganese iron phosphate, ternary material, and lithium manganese oxide.

In alternative embodiments, the metal M may be selected from one or more of Mg, Zn, Al, Ti.

Example 1

Preparation of positive plate

Mixing the following components in parts by weight: 2.5: 2.5 mixing the lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent (SP conductive carbon black) and a binder (PVDF), and adding metal Mg powder in the process, wherein the content of the Mg powder accounts for 0.01 percent of that of the lithium iron phosphate. Coating the slurry on an aluminum foil, and drying to obtain the positive plate for later use.

Preparation of cathode plate

Mixing the following components in parts by weight of 95.5: 1.0: 1.5: 2.0 of artificial graphite, SP conductive carbon black, CMC and SBR are mixed to be slurry, coated on copper foil and dried to obtain a negative plate for later use.

Preparation of the electrolyte

The electrolyte is prepared by mixing Ethylene Carbonate (EC), Ethyl Methyl Carbonate (EMC) and diethyl carbonate (DEC) according to the volume ratio of 1:1:1 to obtain an organic solvent to form an electrolyte, and then fully drying lithium salt LiPF6Dissolving in the mixed organic solvent to prepare electrolyte with lithium salt concentration of 1.1 mol/L.

Assembled into a battery

Assembling the obtained positive plate, the diaphragm and the negative plate into a battery core, placing the battery core in a battery shell, injecting electrolyte into the battery shell, and performing vacuum packaging, standing, formation, shaping and other processes to form the 5Ah battery.

Battery performance testing

The batteries prepared in examples 1 to 24 and comparative examples 1 to 5 were tested, and the specific tests were as follows.

Cycling at 25 ℃: the batteries of examples and comparative examples were subjected to an experiment at 25 ℃ and were first subjected to constant-current constant-voltage charging, 1C constant-current constant-voltage charging to a voltage of V1, and a cutoff current of 0.05C; then constant current discharge is carried out, and the 1C is discharged to V2. The discharge capacity was recorded after 3000 cycles, and the test results are shown in table 1.

the batteries of examples 1 to 24 and comparative examples 1 to 5 were shelled and disassembled, the electrolyte, the positive plate and the negative plate were all immersed in NMP (N-methylpyrrolidone) solvent for 12 to 24 hours, and the leachate was subjected to ICP (inductively coupled plasma) test to obtain MmAnThe test results are shown in table 1.

Comparing the data of examples 1 to 3 and comparative examples 1 to 2 in table 1, it can be seen that when the content of M is 0.01 to 0.2% by weight with respect to the positive electrode active material, the capacity retention rate of the battery at 3000 cycles is significantly improved with respect to the battery without the addition of the metal M.

Comparing the data of examples 1-12, it can be seen that the addition of different metals M to the positive electrode can improve the capacity retention rate of the battery at 3000 cycles. It is proved that the cycle performance and the service life of the battery can be improved by adding the metal M of which the ions can be complexed with the lithium salt anions in the electrolyte.

Comparing the data of examples 2,13-21, it can be seen that the addition of metal M to the positive electrode improved the capacity retention rate for 3000 cycles for each of the batteries with different lithium salts. The addition of the metal M to the positive electrode proves that the capacity retention rate of the lithium ion battery can be improved, so that the cycle performance and the service life are improved.

Comparing the data of examples 2,22-24 and comparative examples 1,3-4, it can be seen that the addition of metal M improves the capacity retention rate of the battery for 3000 cycles for different positive electrode active materials.

From the above data, it can be seen that the cycle performance, especially the long cycle performance, of the battery can be improved by adding the metal M to the positive electrode, so that the service life of the battery can be improved.
